task: A rectangular cantilever beam 300 mm long and 30 mm wide carries a 200 N point load at its free end, and the bending stress may not exceed 60 MPa. Find the minimum beam depth (height), then model the beam as a solid block 300 mm long, 30 mm wide and that deep.

A rectangular cantilever beam 250 mm long and 40 mm wide carries a 500 N point load at its free end, and the bending stress may not exceed 100 MPa. Find the minimum beam depth (height), then model the beam as a solid block 250 mm long, 40 mm wide and that deep.

A rectangular cantilever beam 400 mm long and 20 mm wide carries a 120 N point load at its free end, and the bending stress may not exceed 80 MPa. Find the minimum beam depth (height), then model the beam as a solid block 400 mm long, 20 mm wide and that deep.
A wooden cube (density 600 kg/m^3) floating in fresh water (1000 kg/m^3) must just keep a 2 kg load above the water when fully submerged. Find the cube's side length, then model the cube.
A wooden cube (density 700 kg/m^3) floating in fresh water (1000 kg/m^3) must just keep a 5 kg load above the water when fully submerged. Find the cube's side length, then model the cube.
A wooden cube (density 400 kg/m^3) floating in fresh water (1000 kg/m^3) must just keep a 1.2 kg load above the water when fully submerged. Find the cube's side length, then model the cube.

A copper wire (resistivity 1.68e-08 ohm m) 10 m long carries 5 A, and the voltage drop along it may not exceed 0.25 V. Find the minimum wire diameter, then model a 300 mm long sample of the wire as a solid cylinder of that diameter.

A aluminium wire (resistivity 2.65e-08 ohm m) 20 m long carries 10 A, and the voltage drop along it may not exceed 0.5 V. Find the minimum wire diameter, then model a 300 mm long sample of the wire as a solid cylinder of that diameter.

A copper wire (resistivity 1.68e-08 ohm m) 5 m long carries 20 A, and the voltage drop along it may not exceed 0.1 V. Find the minimum wire diameter, then model a 300 mm long sample of the wire as a solid cylinder of that diameter.

A parallel-plate capacitor with square plates must have a capacitance of 1000 pF, with a dielectric of relative permittivity 4 and a gap of 0.1 mm (vacuum permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m). Find the side of a plate, then model one plate as a square plate with that side, 1 mm thick.

A parallel-plate capacitor with square plates must have a capacitance of 470 pF, with a dielectric of relative permittivity 2.2 and a gap of 0.2 mm (vacuum permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m). Find the side of a plate, then model one plate as a square plate with that side, 1 mm thick.

A parallel-plate capacitor with square plates must have a capacitance of 2200 pF, with a dielectric of relative permittivity 10 and a gap of 0.05 mm (vacuum permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m). Find the side of a plate, then model one plate as a square plate with that side, 1 mm thick.

A square insulating panel 500 mm by 500 mm (thermal conductivity 0.04 W/(m K)) has a 20 K temperature difference across it and may conduct at most 4 W. Find its minimum thickness, then model the panel.

A square insulating panel 300 mm by 300 mm (thermal conductivity 0.8 W/(m K)) has a 15 K temperature difference across it and may conduct at most 54 W. Find its minimum thickness, then model the panel.

A square insulating panel 200 mm by 200 mm (thermal conductivity 1.5 W/(m K)) has a 30 K temperature difference across it and may conduct at most 360 W. Find its minimum thickness, then model the panel.

A cylindrical tank 100 mm in inside diameter must hold 2 mol of an ideal gas at 300 K and 500 kPa (R = 8.314 J/(mol K)). Find the inside height, then model the tank's gas space as a solid cylinder 100 mm in diameter and that tall.

A cylindrical tank 120 mm in inside diameter must hold 1 mol of an ideal gas at 293 K and 200 kPa (R = 8.314 J/(mol K)). Find the inside height, then model the tank's gas space as a solid cylinder 120 mm in diameter and that tall.

A cylindrical tank 80 mm in inside diameter must hold 0.5 mol of an ideal gas at 350 K and 100 kPa (R = 8.314 J/(mol K)). Find the inside height, then model the tank's gas space as a solid cylinder 80 mm in diameter and that tall.
A cylinder faces a 30 m/s airflow end-on (air density 1.225 kg/m^3, drag coefficient 0.8) and must produce 5 N of drag. Find its diameter, then model the cylinder with that diameter and 100 mm long.
A cylinder faces a 25 m/s airflow end-on (air density 1.225 kg/m^3, drag coefficient 1.1) and must produce 12 N of drag. Find its diameter, then model the cylinder with that diameter and 100 mm long.
A cylinder faces a 40 m/s airflow end-on (air density 1.225 kg/m^3, drag coefficient 0.9) and must produce 2 N of drag. Find its diameter, then model the cylinder with that diameter and 100 mm long.

A wing with a lift coefficient of 1.2 flies at 20 m/s in air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 and must lift 600 N. Its span is 8 m; find its chord. Then model a 500 mm long section of the wing as a flat plate 500 mm long, as wide as that chord, and 15 mm thick.

A wing with a lift coefficient of 0.9 flies at 12 m/s in air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 and must lift 250 N. Its span is 5 m; find its chord. Then model a 500 mm long section of the wing as a flat plate 500 mm long, as wide as that chord, and 15 mm thick.

A wing with a lift coefficient of 1.1 flies at 30 m/s in air of density 1.225 kg/m^3 and must lift 1500 N. Its span is 10 m; find its chord. Then model a 500 mm long section of the wing as a flat plate 500 mm long, as wide as that chord, and 15 mm thick.

A plate 50 mm wide carries a 9000 N tensile load across its width, and the stress may not exceed 60 MPa. Find the minimum thickness, then model a plate 120 mm long and 50 mm wide with that thickness and an 8 mm diameter through hole 45 mm from its center at each end, on the long centerline.

A plate 25 mm wide carries a 4000 N tensile load across its width, and the stress may not exceed 40 MPa. Find the minimum thickness, then model a plate 90 mm long and 25 mm wide with that thickness and an 8 mm diameter through hole 30 mm from its center at each end, on the long centerline.

A plate 60 mm wide carries a 15000 N tensile load across its width, and the stress may not exceed 125 MPa. Find the minimum thickness, then model a plate 150 mm long and 60 mm wide with that thickness and an 8 mm diameter through hole 60 mm from its center at each end, on the long centerline.
A solid steel disc (density 7850 kg/m^3) 120 mm in diameter must weigh 2 kg. Find its thickness, then model the disc with that thickness and add a 10 mm diameter through hole at its center.
A solid aluminium disc (density 2700 kg/m^3) 80 mm in diameter must weigh 0.3 kg. Find its thickness, then model the disc with that thickness and add a 10 mm diameter through hole at its center.
A solid copper disc (density 8900 kg/m^3) 90 mm in diameter must weigh 1.5 kg. Find its thickness, then model the disc with that thickness and add a 10 mm diameter through hole at its center.
A solid circular shaft transmits 120 N m of torque, and the shear stress may not exceed 50 MPa. Find the minimum diameter, then model a solid shaft of that diameter and 150 mm long.
A solid circular shaft transmits 30 N m of torque, and the shear stress may not exceed 25 MPa. Find the minimum diameter, then model a solid shaft of that diameter and 100 mm long.
A solid circular shaft transmits 400 N m of torque, and the shear stress may not exceed 60 MPa. Find the minimum diameter, then model a solid shaft of that diameter and 200 mm long.

A copper bar must carry 500 A at a current density of 2.5 A/mm^2. It is 40 mm wide; find its thickness. Then model the bar, 200 mm long and 40 mm wide with that thickness, with a 6 mm diameter through hole at its center.

A copper bar must carry 150 A at a current density of 1.5 A/mm^2. It is 20 mm wide; find its thickness. Then model the bar, 120 mm long and 20 mm wide with that thickness, with a 6 mm diameter through hole at its center.

A copper bar must carry 800 A at a current density of 4 A/mm^2. It is 50 mm wide; find its thickness. Then model the bar, 250 mm long and 50 mm wide with that thickness, with a 6 mm diameter through hole at its center.
A hydraulic piston must produce 50 kN at an oil pressure of 15 MPa. Find the piston diameter, then model it as a solid cylinder of that diameter and 80 mm long.
A hydraulic piston must produce 8 kN at an oil pressure of 5 MPa. Find the piston diameter, then model it as a solid cylinder of that diameter and 50 mm long.
A hydraulic piston must produce 120 kN at an oil pressure of 20 MPa. Find the piston diameter, then model it as a solid cylinder of that diameter and 100 mm long.
A simple pendulum must have a period of 2 s where g = 9.81 m/s^2. Find its length, then model the pendulum rod as a solid cylinder 8 mm in diameter with that length.
